title: Reactor servo and regulatory objectives
equipment: Jacketed stirred reactor, product-temperature transmitter, and jacket heating valve
physicalPurpose: Track production-temperature changes and reject cold-feed heat-load changes with one explicitly evaluated PI loop.
principalTechnique: Separate servo and regulatory experiments with IAE, ISE, ITAE, transient, and actuator measures
objective: Distinguish setpoint and load paths, calculate objective-specific metrics, and demonstrate that one unchanged tuning can pass regulatory requirements while failing servo overshoot.

simplifications: The well-mixed reactor and jacket are represented by one local thermal state.
The five-degree output-balance event is the equivalent thermal effect of colder feed, not a physical feed-temperature measurement.
Reaction heat, composition dynamics, fouling, valve nonlinearity and independent trips are omitted.

baseline.limitation: The regulatory-focused PI produces servo overshoot above the declared 1.0 degC requirement when full proportional action responds to the setpoint step.

change.decision: Restore the same initial condition, hold SP fixed, and apply the independent load without changing controller, plant, limits, timing, or seed.

disturbances: A separate fresh servo run steps SP from 80 to 85 degC and ends before the load event
The regulatory run holds SP at 80 degC and applies the load at 60 s

acceptance.window: 5.1 through 55.0 s after the 80 to 85 degC setpoint step
60.1 through 120.0 s; absolute error must enter 0.5 degC and remain there

abortPredicates: SP, PV or MV is nonfinite
PV or MV leaves its hard limit
Controller mode leaves Auto during a run
Controller parameters, plant, initial state, limits, timing or seed differ between objective runs
safety.restorationMode: Request Manual zero after the automatic observation and retain each rate-constrained update until the applied valve reaches zero
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The setpoint and cold-feed-equivalent experiments are simulation evidence and do not authorise physical reactor actions.

video.viewerOutcome: Separate servo and regulatory experiments, calculate their metrics, and explain why one unchanged PI can pass one objective while failing another.
requiredVisibleEvidence: IAE ISE ITAE equations and units
two separate traces and metric tables
0.5 degC settling band with 0.01 degC comparison tolerance

learning.context: The previous lessons handled controller structure and actuator constraints, but judging one event does not qualify a loop that must both track production changes and reject process loads.
learning.reason: Setpoint and disturbance changes enter through different paths, so the same PI can satisfy one objective and violate another; each needs separate requirements and evidence.
theory: A servo test changes setpoint and measures reference tracking, while a regulatory test holds setpoint fixed and changes a disturbance.
IAE sums absolute error times dt, ISE sums squared error times dt, and ITAE weights absolute error by elapsed time before summing.
Overshoot, settling or recovery time and total absolute actuator travel capture different accuracy, dynamic and equipment costs.
Every metric requires a named event, window, engineering unit, tolerance and requirement; mixing servo and regulatory windows invalidates the comparison.
learning.workedPrediction: The -5 degC load equivalent needs 5/0.25 = 20 percent more steady valve. For a 5 degC setpoint step, Kp 8 and b=1 contribute 40 percent immediate proportional demand, predicting fast response with overshoot risk.
practicalPreparation: Inspect the reactor, transmitter, heating valve, cold-feed load, signal units, 80 degC and 50 percent operating point, limits and safe state.
Define the two fresh runs and all metric windows, calculate the steady load correction and initial servo P demand, and verify equivalent settings before approval.
learning.baseline: Run the fresh 80 to 85 degC servo experiment and calculate overshoot, settling, IAE, ISE, ITAE and valve travel.
learning.change: Restore initial state, hold SP at 80 degC and apply the -5 degC cold-feed equivalent at 60 s without changing PI, plant, timing, limits or seed.
learning.comparison: Compare objective-specific metric tables and explicitly mark the 1.0 degC servo overshoot requirement failed and the 40 s regulatory recovery requirement passed.
learning.validation: Confirm 1.05 degC servo overshoot fails its 1.0 degC requirement; the reported 19.7 s servo settling diagnostic uses its declared 0.1 s reproduction tolerance; 1.28 degC regulatory excitation, 11.6 s recovery and 0.004 degC final-window mean absolute error pass their requirements; the 0.5 degC settling band uses its declared 0.01 degC numerical comparison tolerance; diagnostic integral and travel measures are finite; PV and applied MV remain bounded; and both runs retain the complete Manual-zero restoration.
learning.explanation: Explain that aggressive regulatory tuning is valuable for load rejection but full proportional setpoint response causes the servo failure, creating a precise reason for Lesson 12 setpoint weighting.
learning.transfer: For another loop, specify separate servo and regulatory experiments, compute objective-specific error and actuator metrics from equivalent fresh runs, and state which requirements pass or fail without collapsing them into one score.
